public_rationale: Marcus said almost every recent LLM was trained on roughly the same internet data, and that this is why models cluster near the middle. Mozilla published a report in February 2024 that reviewed 47 LLMs released from 2019 to October 2023. It found that at least 64% were trained on Common Crawl (e1). That shows many models share one major source. It does not show that their training data was roughly the same overall. The review also does not cover models released after October 2023. On the cause, no study in the evidence links shared pretraining data to models' views converging. Rozado's February 2024 preprint gives preliminary evidence that political preferences may be embedded mostly during fine-tuning or reinforcement learning, not pretraining (e2). That points away from shared pretraining data as the main cause. The author says the result is not conclusive. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is clearly met, so the outcome is unresolved.
limitations: The training data of major 2024–2025 models is largely undisclosed, so the evidence cannot measure their overlap.
Using a common source such as Common Crawl does not measure how much the full training sets overlap.
The only evidence bearing on the cause is one preliminary preprint. No controlled study isolates shared pretraining data as the cause.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So far, almost every recent LLM has been trained on roughly the same internet data, and this is why models cluster near the middle in their views.

statement.excerpt: Necessity has (heretofore) meant that pretty much every recent LLM has been trained on more less the same data.

from_speaker: trained on more or less the same data
every bit of data they can scrape from the internet
explains why models cluster not far from the middle
our_interpretation: The claim has two parts. First, almost all recent major LLMs were trained on largely overlapping web data. Second, that shared data is why their views cluster near the middle.
'Heretofore' covers roughly 2020 to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Documentation shows that nearly all recent major LLMs draw heavily on the same web corpora, and studies link shared pretraining data to the convergence of their expressed views.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documentation shows that recent major LLMs use largely different data, or studies show the convergence in views comes mainly from post-training rather than shared pretraining data.

evidence.excerpt: the study analyzed 47 LLMs published between 2019 and October 2023 that power text generators and found at least 64% of them were trained on Common Crawl.
evidence.explanation: Shows that many LLMs share a major data source, which partly supports the overlap claim. But 64% is short of 'pretty much every', the review stops at 2023, and it does not test any effect on views.

evidence.excerpt: our results provide preliminary evidence for the intriguing hypothesis that the embedding of political preferences into LLMs might be happening mostly post-pretraining.
evidence.explanation: Preliminary evidence that the shared political lean comes mainly from fine-tuning, not shared pretraining data. This cuts against Marcus's explanation, but the author says it is not conclusive.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Training-data disclosures for the major 2024–2025 models, and controlled studies that compare the views of models pretrained on different corpora but given the same fine-tuning.
